title: Building the Church begins with the worth of souls
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Fayette, New York, in the first part of June 1829. It came after David Whitmer’s baptism and before a 14 June letter from Oliver Cowdery. It answers something Oliver wanted to know and speaks to him and David Whitmer. Joseph later said it made known the calling of twelve apostles and how to build up the Church. Later that month Oliver drafted “Articles of the Church of Christ,” drawn largely from the Book of Mormon.
summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery that what he has written is true and commands him to rely on it. It says the written record holds the foundation of the Church and gospel. It confirms Oliver’s baptism by Joseph Smith and says Joseph is called for the Lord’s purpose. It calls Oliver and David Whitmer to cry repentance, with the same calling as Paul. It explains that the worth of souls is great because the Redeemer suffered for all. It describes the joy of bringing even one soul to Christ. It then speaks of twelve disciples who will take Christ’s name, preach, and baptize. Oliver and David are told to search out the Twelve by their desires and works.

contextNote.title: Why one soul matters so much
contextNote.text: Oliver and David were being called to preach before any church yet existed. Verse 10 says “the worth of souls is great” in the sight of God. Verses 11–12 explain that worth by the Redeemer’s suffering for all people and his rising again. Verse 13 adds that he has great joy in each person who repents. Verses 15–16 then turn that joy into a measure for the preachers’ own lives. A whole lifetime would be worth it for even one soul. In this passage, a soul’s “worth” is set by what Christ paid for it.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 18, “The Worth of Souls Is Great,” teaches that every person matters to God. Verses 10–16 move from Christ’s suffering to the preacher’s joy; whose soul could you help this week, and how?
reviewNote: Read all 47 verses. Official heading gives Fayette, June 1829, to Joseph Smith, Oliver Cowdery, and David Whitmer, with Joseph’s note on the twelve apostles. JSP historical introduction read for the early June dating, Cowdery’s June 1829 Articles, and the 1835 selection of the Twelve as its fulfillment. JSP notes it is unclear whether “disciples” and “apostles” were treated as the same in 1829. Paul is named in verse 9 but was not added as a person. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
